target_customer: Consumers who have already taken a DNA test at Ancestry, 23andMe or MyHeritage and want more analysis, plus genealogy hobbyists
problem: People with raw DNA data from one testing service could not easily get more ancestry, trait and matching insights without buying another test.
business_model: Consumer freemium with paid reports and subscriptions for DNA apps; later a genealogy product (YourRoots)
product_category: Consumer genomics and genealogy app platform

founders.name: Tomohiro Takano
founders.background_notes: Berkeley SkyDeck says he started the project in Japan in 2016 as a weekend project with co-founders he met at university, then moved to the Bay Area.

founders.name: Kensuke Numakura
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as co-founder and CTO; no background given.

competitors.name: Promethease
competitors.what: Paid health report from uploaded raw DNA files

competitors.name: GEDmatch
competitors.what: Free raw DNA upload for genealogy matching

technical_complexity.rationale: Parsing raw genotype files, building ancestry and trait models from public studies and handling sensitive genetic data securely is standard data engineering with some hard science and privacy work.

defensibility.rationale: Raw DNA upload sites were numerous and the underlying data belongs to the user and the test provider, so switching was easy. Accumulated user DNA and matches add some value.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The big testing companies kept their own ancestry and traits products. No source shows them copying the DNA app store idea.

market_need_then: The YC page cites more than 50 million people in the US having tested their DNA, a large installed base of raw data files that people could reuse.

branding.name_origin: A profile of the company says the name was chosen to describe the product, a link between a person and their genome.
branding.domain_note: Uses genomelink.io, not an exact .com; the genealogy brand uses yourroots.com.

rebrands.why: Launched as a separate genealogy brand starting with YourRoots Map, per the company press release of July 1, 2025

brand_strength.rationale: Reviews exist on third-party blogs and the GENOMELINK trademark was registered in January 2021, but no source shows strong community, mascot or viral growth.

outcome_analysis: Genomelink is still active after nearly a decade, expanding from consumer DNA reports to a separate genealogy brand, YourRoots, launched in July 2025. Funding is only visible through conflicting aggregator data, so its financial trajectory is unclear. It shows steady survival in a small consumer niche without a visible breakout.
notes: Funding unverified: Seedtable shows a 454K seed in 2017 (led by 500 Startups Japan per its description), StartupBlink and Persana describe about 4M seed from Berkeley SkyDeck, Sony and Japanese VCs, CB Insights shows 4.49M over 7 rounds with a Seed II in 2023-07, Caplight shows 23M. All aggregators, none confirmed by a company or press source, so no round is recorded. Competitors come from the company's own 2019 Medium post, so this is a self-published source. YC page lists founded 2017; SkyDeck says 2016 start.
